data.name: Rhythm drill (working name)
data.pitch: A warm-up drill where targets arrive on the beat of a song, either your own uploaded track or a built-in one, and you aim and shoot them in time. It should feel close to Beat Saber: flowing, musical and a bit hypnotic, not like a test.
data.problem: The current daily warm-up is seven separate drills with a briefing and score screen between each. It works, but it feels like work and starts cold. A rhythm drill gives the hands a steady, repeatable pace to settle into, and gives players a warm-up they actually want to start.
data.audience: Azimuth players: Overwatch players from beginner to intermediate, on desktop with a mouse (mostly Chromium), who already use the daily warm-up and want to bring their own music.
data.whyNow: v3 added a positional audio engine and a mature drill, level and coach framework, so a music-driven drill can reuse most of what exists.
data.successLooksLike: You'd choose it over the plain warm-up. Load a song, notes land on the beat, and after a few minutes your hand feels loose and accurate.

items.text: TypeScript (strict; build runs tsc --noEmit) + Vite 8 + three.js 0.186. No UI framework: screens are template-string HTML in src/ui.
Every drill extends Drill (src/drills/drill.ts), returns a DrillReport (0–100 score, stats, analytics) and is registered in DRILL_DEFS (src/drills/registry.ts) with 10 levels and 1/2/3★ thresholds.
All sound goes through the single WebAudio Audio class (src/core/audio.ts), unlocked from a user gesture. Today it only synthesises sounds; it does not play samples or music files yet.
Static site on GitHub Pages: no server and no accounts. Uploaded audio never leaves the browser.
Desktop Chromium is the main target (pointer lock with unadjustedMovement). Firefox must still work.
Saves are small JSON in localStorage via store (src/core/store.ts), with backup export/import in Settings → Your data. Audio files cannot be stored there (~5 MB limit).
Shots resolve at the instant of the click (ShotResult.at on the game clock, which freezes while paused), not on the next frame.
Tests are vitest in a node environment (tests/*.test.ts). Beat detection, chart building and scoring must be pure functions that run without WebAudio or the DOM.
No copyrighted music in the repo. Any built-in track must be generated or original.
All copy is in plain words for beginners, in the same voice as the coach and Field Manual.

flowchart LR
  F["Audio file: mp3, ogg, wav"] --> DB[("IndexedDB song library")]
  DB --> DEC["Decode with WebAudio"]
  DEC --> AN["Beat analysis: tempo + onsets"]
  AN --> CH["Chart builder"]
  CH --> RD["RhythmDrill extends Drill"]
  DEC --> PL["Music playback on the AudioContext clock"]
  PL -. "sync" .-> RD
  RD --> REP["DrillReport"]
  REP --> UI["Debrief, Logbook, Daily warm-up"]
data.caption: Proposed flow: an uploaded audio file is stored in IndexedDB, decoded with WebAudio, and analysed offline for tempo and note onsets (a pure function). A chart builder turns that into notes on the beat. RhythmDrill (a normal Drill subclass) plays the music on the AudioContext clock, positions notes from that clock, and reports through the usual DrillReport into the debrief, Logbook and daily warm-up.

data.risk: Notes drift out of sync with the music. The game clock runs on requestAnimationFrame and freezes on pause, while music plays on the AudioContext clock, and output latency (especially Bluetooth headphones) adds 20–250 ms.
data.mitigation: Position every note from AudioContext.currentTime minus outputLatency, never from accumulated frame time. Pausing suspends the AudioContext. Add a one-time audio offset calibration (tap along to a click) stored in settings, plus a manual offset slider.

sides.label: Fully automatic
sides.summary: The drill detects the tempo and beats and places targets on the beat grid, with busier patterns in louder parts of the song. Drop a song in and play.
pros: Fastest: playing within seconds of upload
No extra screens
cons: Some songs get the wrong tempo (live recordings, swing, tempo changes), and then every target is off-beat with no way to fix it

sides.label: Automatic + quick fix (recommended)

data.risk: Automatic analysis picks the wrong tempo or beat phase on some songs (live recordings, swing, tempo changes, long quiet intros), so targets feel off-beat and there's no way for the player to fix it.
data.mitigation: Use onset-strength autocorrelation with a tempo prior (prefer 80–180 BPM, resolving half and double tempo) and track beats per section rather than one global grid. Score the analysis confidence; when it's low, place targets on detected onsets (audible hits) instead of a strict grid. Test against generated songs with swing, tempo ramps and noise in vitest.

data.statement: Drop in a song and be playing it within seconds, with no setup.
data.why: Bringing your own music is the hook. Any friction before the first target kills it as a warm-up.
checks: Uploading an MP3, WAV or OGG file (plus M4A/AAC on Chromium) starts analysis immediately; an unsupported or broken file shows a plain-words error instead of failing silently.
A 4-minute song is analysed in under 5 s on a mid-range laptop, and the page never freezes for more than 100 ms while it runs.
Uploaded songs are stored in the browser (IndexedDB) and are still in the song list after a reload, with no re-upload.
The same song at the same level always produces the same chart, so scores are comparable between runs.

data.statement: Targets land on the beat of the music.
data.why: If timing feels off, it's not a rhythm drill, and an automatic chart has no fix-up step (D3).
checks: On generated test songs (drum loops at 70–190 BPM, with swing, noise and a quiet intro), detected tempo is within 1% and beat times within 20 ms of the truth (vitest, node).
During play, every target's spawn and hit time is computed from the AudioContext clock; drift between chart and audio stays under 10 ms across a 4-minute song.
Pausing stops music and targets together, and resuming continues in sync.
An audio offset (from a short tap-along calibration or set by hand) shifts every target; after calibration, the player's taps average within ±20 ms of the beat.

data.statement: Six target types each spawn on the beat, behave in time with the music and vanish if missed.
data.why: A mix of target types is the core idea (D1, D2): each one trains a different aim skill inside one musical run.
checks: Flick shapes, strafers, holds, bursts, peekers and decoys all appear in charts.
Every target spawns on a beat (or eighth beat for bursts) and is removed when its hit window ends without a hit.
Strafers change direction on beats; holds move along their path in step with the beat; peekers show and hide on beats.

data.question: How are charts generated so that any song gets a good chart?
data.outcome: Each song is analysed for its structure (beats, bars, sections, energy, onsets). A themed preset supplies a probabilistic decision matrix: for each section kind it weights which target types spawn and how densely. The generator samples spawns bar by bar from that matrix, seeded by song + level + preset so the same inputs always give the same chart. Adding a new song needs no hand-made chart.
data.rationale: The human's comment on V3: in the long run there will be many songs, so chart generation must work independently per song, from the song's own structure, using a probabilistic decision matrix with basic themed presets.
consequences: Song analysis must find sections, not only beats.
Presets are data (a matrix per preset), not code, so new ones are cheap to add.
Levels scale the preset's output (density, window, size, allowed types) rather than needing separate matrices.

data.source:
flowchart LR
  S[Song] --> A["Analysis: beats, bars, energy, onsets"]
  A --> SEG["Sections: intro, calm, build, peak, outro"]
  SEG --> G[Generator]
  A --> G
  P["Preset matrix"] --> G
  L["Level: density, window, size, types"] --> G
  R["Seed: song + level + preset"] --> G
  G --> C["Chart: timed targets"]
data.caption: Proposed chart generator. The song analysis yields the beat grid, bars, per-beat energy and onset strength, and splits the song into sections classified as intro, calm, build, peak or outro. For each bar, the generator takes that bar's section kind, looks up the preset matrix row for it (target-type weights and density), scales it by the level (density, hit window, target size, which types are allowed), and samples spawns with a seeded random generator. Spawns snap to the strongest onsets in the bar. The output is a chart: a list of timed targets with type, position and parameters.

data.title: Define Overdrive's song, analysis and chart types
data.description: src/rhythm/types.ts. SongMeta (id = content hash, name, duration, preset, difficulty, addedAt); Analysis (bpm, beats in seconds, downbeats, per-beat energy, onset envelope, confidence); Section {startBar, endBar, kind: intro|calm|build|peak|outro}; Preset (rows per section kind: type weights + targets per bar, plus target params); Difficulty easy|normal|hard|expert; ChartTarget as a union on kind (flick with shape circle|diamond|triangle, burst, strafer, hold, peeker, decoy), each with launchTime, landTime, targetTime, windowEnd, position (bearing, pitch, distance) and per-kind params; Chart {songId, preset, level, targets, walls}.
doneWhen: src/rhythm/types.ts exports the types above and `npm run typecheck` passes.
Type and field names follow the glossary (Song, Chart, Target, Section, Style preset, Difficulty, Target beat, Hit window).

data.title: Write a test-only song generator with known beats and sections
data.description: tests/helpers/songgen.ts: a pure, seeded function (bpm, sampleRate, bars, section energies, swing, noise level, quiet intro, optional tempo ramp) → { pcm: Float32Array, beats: number[], sections }. Kick, snare and hat from sine and noise envelopes. Test fixture only (D11).
doneWhen: Generates deterministic loops from 70 to 190 BPM, with swing, noise and a quiet intro, plus the true beat times and section boundaries.
Nothing under src/ imports it, and it is not bundled by `npm run build`.

data.title: Detect tempo, beats and onsets from PCM
data.description: src/rhythm/analysis.ts: analyse(pcm: mono Float32Array, sampleRate) → Analysis. Spectral-flux onset envelope (~10 ms hop); tempo by autocorrelation with a prior preferring 80–180 BPM and resolving half/double tempo; dynamic-programming beat tracking so local drift is followed; per-beat RMS energy; a confidence score. No DOM or WebAudio.
doneWhen: vitest: on songgen loops at 70–190 BPM, including swing, noise and an 8 s quiet intro, tempo is within 1% and at least 95% of beats fall within 20 ms of the truth.
A 4-minute 44.1 kHz mono song is analysed in under 3 s in node.
Beatless noise input returns low confidence rather than a confident wrong tempo.

data.title: Split songs into bars and sections by energy
data.description: src/rhythm/sections.ts: estimate downbeats from the accent pattern across the four beat phases, build bars, smooth bar energy, find change points and classify energy tiers as intro, calm, build, peak or outro. Sections are at least 4 bars and bar-aligned; fall back to energy-only tiers when change points are weak.
doneWhen: On songgen songs with known quiet/loud structure, section boundaries are within 1 bar of the truth and kinds match.
A flat loop yields valid sections (no crash, at least one non-intro section).
Every section is at least 4 bars and starts on a bar boundary.

data.title: Add the preset format, the Mixed preset and the level table
data.description: src/rhythm/presets.ts: the Preset data format and MIXED (start from V5's numbers). src/rhythm/levels.ts: per level 1–10 a density multiplier, hit window (beats), Perfect width (ms), target radius, strafer speed and health, hold length, peek time and cue strength; difficulty bands Easy 1–3, Normal 4–6, Hard 7–8, Expert 9–10; levelFor(difficulty, unlockedLevel) implementing D10.
doneWhen: Each Mixed row's weights sum to 1 (test).
levelFor matches D10 for all 4 difficulties × unlocked levels 1–10 (test).
Across levels the hit window and Perfect width never grow and density never drops (test).
Only Mixed is listed as a selectable preset (D8).

data.title: Generate seeded charts from analysis, preset and level
data.description: src/rhythm/generator.ts: generate(analysis, sections, preset, level, songId) → Chart. PRNG (e.g. mulberry32) seeded by hash(songId, preset, level). Per bar: look up the section row, draw a target count from targets-per-bar × level density, choose beat slots weighted by onset strength (bursts use eighth notes), sample each type from the row weights, and place it: on-screen angles for most types, 60–150° off-screen for triangles (D14), cover walls for peekers. Cap concurrent targets per level; tracking types (strafers, holds) never overlap each other. Charts end per D12.
doneWhen: The same inputs give a deep-equal chart; a different songId gives a different one.
Over a 200-bar synthetic song, type frequencies per section kind are within ±5% of the preset matrix.
Every target's targetTime lies on a beat (an eighth for bursts) within 1 ms.
Concurrent targets never exceed the level's cap, and no two tracking-type targets overlap in time.

data.title: Judge hits, track the combo and compute the 0–100 score
data.description: src/rhythm/scoring.ts: judge(hitTime, target, level) → perfect | early | late | miss plus a signed offset in ms (D4: any hit in the window counts, Perfect within the Perfect width of the target beat). Combo and multiplier (Perfect builds faster); a decoy hit breaks the combo and costs points; tracking types score the fraction of their life spent on target while firing. Final 0–100 score plus stats: mean signed offset, hit rate per target type and max combo.
doneWhen: Unit tests cover perfect, early, late and miss at the window and Perfect boundaries.
Perfect hits raise the combo multiplier faster than early or late hits (test).
A decoy hit resets the combo (test).
The score stays within 0–100 and never drops when a miss becomes a hit (test).

data.description: src/drills/overdrive.ts: class OverdriveDrill extends Drill (id 'overdrive', movable = false, D13). Clicks go to scoring; held fire damages tracking types while on target (D13). report() returns a DrillReport with analytics.flicks for flick-type targets (via FlickRecorder) and rhythm stats.

Each target launches within one frame of its chart time and vanishes at its window end if not hit.

data.title: Add tap targets: flick shapes, bursts and decoys
data.description: src/drills/overdrive-targets.ts. Per D14: circle = normal on-screen flick, diamond = small precision target with a bigger Perfect bonus, triangle = off-screen wide flick that points the way to turn, with a positional ping (TargetSound). Bursts: 3–5 small orbs on consecutive eighth notes along a line or arc. Decoys: a friendly-coloured figure; hitting one breaks the combo. Hitboxes match the visible shapes.

data.question: How do levels unlock inside a difficulty?
data.outcome: Each difficulty band unlocks on its own. You start a band at its lowest level, and a star on a level unlocks the next level in that band (Easy 1→2→3, Hard 7→8, and so on). The level played is the highest unlocked level in the chosen band. Other drills' progression is unchanged.

options.summary: Stars unlock the next level within the band.

options.summary: Keep Azimuth's rule: only consecutive stars from level 1 unlock.

data.rationale: Azimuth's unlockedLevel() only counts stars on consecutive levels from level 1, so under D10 stars earned on Hard or Expert would never unlock anything until every lower level had a star. Per-band unlocking keeps D10's "all difficulties open" meaningful.

data.question: Do you have to hit on the beat, or just before the target is gone?
data.outcome: Window + beat bonus. A target appears on a beat and stays for a hit window. Any hit inside the window counts, but a hit close to the target's own beat scores Perfect and builds the combo faster. Higher levels shrink the window towards the beat.

options.label: On the beat
options.summary: Exact beat, ±60 ms graded; else a miss.

options.label: Before it's gone
options.summary: Any hit in the window counts; sooner scores more.

options.label: Window + beat bonus
options.summary: Any hit in the window counts; on-beat hits score Perfect.

data.rationale: Chosen by the human: rhythm feel without punishing the stop-then-click habit the coach teaches.
consequences: Judgement words are Perfect (within the Perfect width of the target beat), Early (in the window, before that), Late (in the window, after it) and Miss (window ended).

data.question: How are charts generated so that any song gets a good chart?
data.outcome: Each song is analysed for its structure (beats, bars, sections, energy, onsets). When you add a song you choose presets that shape how its chart is built: a style preset (a probabilistic matrix weighting target types and density per section kind) and a difficulty (D9). The generator samples spawns bar by bar from the style matrix, scaled by the level the difficulty resolves to, seeded by song + preset + level so the same inputs always give the same chart. No song needs a hand-made chart. The MVP ships one style preset, Mixed (D8); the others are on the roadmap.
data.rationale: The human's comments on V3 and D7: many songs in the long run, so charts must be generated from each song's own structure via a probabilistic decision matrix, with a few basic presets picked when adding a song to alter how it's structured. Start with one preset for the MVP so it can be tested, and keep the rest on the roadmap.
consequences: Song analysis must find sections, not only beats.
Presets are data: one matrix per preset, plus optional multipliers on the level table's target parameters (e.g. strafer health × 1.5 for a future Tracker preset).
The seed uses the level, not the difficulty, because the level inside a band changes as you unlock (D17).
Adding a song shows a preset picker; with only Mixed in the MVP it defaults to Mixed so adding stays one step.
Roadmap presets: Quick taps, Tracker, Incoming (see scope, later).

data.risk: Notes drift out of sync with the music. The game clock runs on requestAnimationFrame and freezes on pause, while music plays on the AudioContext clock, and output latency (especially Bluetooth headphones) adds 20–250 ms.
data.mitigation: Position every target from song time (AudioContext time minus output latency minus the audio offset), never from accumulated frame time. Pausing stops the music source and freezes song time; it does not suspend the shared AudioContext, so menu sounds keep working. A tap-along calibration and a manual slider set the audio offset.

terms.meaning: The drill this plan builds (drill id 'overdrive').
An audio file the player added to their library. There is no built-in song (D11).
One pulse of the song's tempo (a quarter note in 4/4). Targets spawn and must be hit relative to beats.
A group of beats, normally four. The generator works bar by bar.
A stretch of the song (at least 4 bars, endBar exclusive). Intro and outro are positional (the first and last sections only); middle sections are classified by energy as calm, build or peak.
The timed list of targets (and walls) for one song at one preset and level. `Chart` in code.
Data that shapes a chart: target-type weights and targets per bar for each section kind, flick shape split, and optional multipliers on target parameters. `Preset` in code. MVP: Mixed only.
Easy, Normal, Hard or Expert, chosen per song. Maps to a band of drill levels (1–3, 4–6, 7–8, 9–10) that unlocks on its own (D17).
The drill's 1–10 step, as in every Azimuth drill. The chart is built at one level inside the chosen difficulty's band.
One thing to shoot that the chart spawns: a flick shape, strafer, hold, burst, peeker or decoy. `ChartTarget` in a chart.
A kind of target with its own look and behaviour (D2). `kind` on ChartTarget.
The beat a target should be hit on. `targetTime` in code (seconds of song time).
From landTime (the target lands) to windowEnd. Any hit inside counts; when it ends without a hit the target is missed and removed.
How a hit is graded: Perfect (within the Perfect width of the target beat), Early or Late (elsewhere in the window), or Miss.
Seconds into the song as the player hears it: AudioContext time since the music started, minus output latency, minus the audio offset. Everything in a run is timed from it.
The four ways the beat is shown (D5): fly-in, closing ring, pulse and the beat strip.
The Guitar Hero-style HUD strip at the bottom of the screen where icons of upcoming targets scroll to a hit line.
How late the player hears the audio, in ms. It is subtracted in song time, so a positive offset makes targets arrive later. Set by the tap-along calibration or by hand.

items.text: TypeScript (strict; build runs tsc --noEmit) + Vite 8 + three.js 0.186. No UI framework: screens are template-string HTML in src/ui.
Every drill extends Drill (src/drills/drill.ts), returns a DrillReport (0–100 score, stats, analytics) and is registered in DRILL_DEFS (src/drills/registry.ts) with 10 levels and 1/2/3★ thresholds.
All sound goes through the single WebAudio Audio class (src/core/audio.ts), unlocked from a user gesture. Today it only synthesises sounds; it does not play samples or music files yet.
Static site on GitHub Pages: no server and no accounts. Uploaded audio never leaves the browser.
Desktop Chromium is the main target (pointer lock with unadjustedMovement). Firefox must still work.
Saves are small JSON in localStorage via store (src/core/store.ts), with backup export/import in Settings → Your data. Audio files cannot be stored there (~5 MB limit).
Shots resolve at the instant of the click: Game.button() calls fire() and then drill.onShot() synchronously inside the mousedown handler (ShotResult.at is game-clock time).
Tests are vitest in a node environment (tests/*.test.ts). Beat detection, chart building and scoring must be pure functions that run without WebAudio or the DOM.
No copyrighted music in the repo. There is no built-in song; test audio is generated by a test-only helper (D11).
All copy is in plain words for beginners, in the same voice as the coach and Field Manual.

data.title: Define Overdrive's song, analysis and chart types
data.description: src/rhythm/types.ts holds types only, plus `as const` lists DIFFICULTIES, SECTION_KINDS, TARGET_KINDS and FLICK_SHAPES. SongMeta {id: SHA-256 hex of the file bytes, name: file name without extension, mime, duration: seconds, addedAt: ISO string, preset: PresetId, difficulty}. Analysis (T3) {version, sampleRate, duration, bpm, beats: number[] seconds, beatEnergy: number[], onsetEnv: Float32Array, onsetHop: seconds per envelope frame, confidence: 0..1}. It has no downbeats. Structure (T4) {downbeats: number[], bars: number[] bar start times, sections: Section[]} with Section {startBar, endBar (exclusive), kind}. PresetRow {weights: Record<TargetKind, number>, perBar: {from, to}}, Preset {id, name, rows: Record<SectionKind, PresetRow>, flickShapes: Record<FlickShape, number>, params?: multipliers}. ChartTarget is a union on kind; every target has launchTime, landTime, targetTime, windowEnd (seconds of song time) and position {bearing, pitch, distance}. Bearing is in degrees clockwise, matching dirFrom() in src/drills/common.ts; pitch is in degrees up; distance is in metres. For figures (strafer, peeker, decoy), position is the ground point and pitch is ignored. FlickTarget adds shape; BurstTarget adds orbs: {time, position}[] and counts as one target in density; Strafer, Hold and Peeker add their params. Wall {bearing, distance, width, height}. Chart {songId, preset, difficulty, level, duration, targets, walls}.
doneWhen: src/rhythm/types.ts exports everything above and `npm run typecheck` passes.
Comments on each type cite the glossary term it implements (Song, Chart, Style preset, Target, Target beat, Hit window).

data.title: Detect tempo, beats and onsets from PCM
data.description: src/rhythm/analysis.ts: analyse(pcm: mono Float32Array, sampleRate) → Analysis (T1; no downbeats, which belong to T4). Spectral-flux onset envelope (~10 ms hop) using a small radix-2 FFT written in src/rhythm/fft.ts, with no new npm packages. Tempo by autocorrelation with a prior preferring 80–180 BPM and resolving half/double tempo; dynamic-programming beat tracking so local drift is followed; per-beat RMS energy; a 0..1 confidence. Export ANALYSIS_VERSION = 1 and stamp it on every Analysis. No DOM or WebAudio.
doneWhen: vitest: on songgen loops at 70–190 BPM, including swing, noise and an 8 s quiet intro, tempo is within 1% and at least 95% of beats fall within 20 ms of the truth.
A 4-minute 44.1 kHz mono song is analysed in under 3 s in node.
Beatless noise returns confidence below 0.4; every songgen loop returns at least 0.6.
package.json dependencies are unchanged.

data.title: Split songs into bars and sections by energy
data.description: src/rhythm/sections.ts: structure(analysis) → Structure (T1). Estimate downbeats from the accent pattern across the four beat phases, build bars, smooth bar energy and find change points. The first section is always intro and the last always outro; middle sections are classified by energy tier as calm, build (rising) or peak. Sections are at least 4 bars, bar-aligned, with endBar exclusive. Fall back to energy-only tiers when change points are weak (R4). The worker (T9) caches Analysis and Structure together.

Every section is at least 4 bars and starts on a bar boundary.

data.title: Add the preset format, the Mixed preset and the level table
data.description: src/rhythm/presets.ts: MIXED, with the matrix, targets per bar and flick shape split exactly as in V5's caption. src/rhythm/levels.ts: LEVELS[1..10] with starting values to be tuned in T19, interpolating linearly between L1 and L10: leadBeats (land → target beat) 2.0→1.0; afterBeats (target beat → window end) 1.5→0.5; perfectMs (± around the target beat) 90→45; density multiplier 0.5→1.25; maxConcurrent 2→5; target radius 0.40→0.24 m (diamonds ×0.6); strafer speed (StyleTuning.speed) 0.6→1.0; strafer health 60→160; strafer life 8 beats; hold length 4→2 beats; peeker shows for 1 beat. Fly-in is always 1 beat. Effective target params = level value × preset multiplier (default 1). Difficulty bands: Easy 1–3, Normal 4–6, Hard 7–8, Expert 9–10. unlockedInBand(progress, difficulty) implements D17 (the band's first level, plus one per consecutive starred level from there, capped at the band's top); levelFor(difficulty, progress) returns that level (D10 + D17).

levelFor gives 7 for Hard with no stars, 8 after a star on 7, and never leaves the band (test).

data.title: Generate seeded charts from analysis, preset and level
data.description: src/rhythm/generator.ts: generate(analysis, structure, preset, level, songId) → Chart. PRNG (e.g. mulberry32) seeded by hash(songId, preset id, level). For each bar: take the section row, draw a count from perBar (ramped across build sections) × level density, choose slots weighted by onset strength (on beats; burst orbs on eighths), and sample each type from the row weights and each flick's shape from the shape split. Times: targetTime = the slot; landTime = targetTime − leadBeats; launchTime = landTime − 1 beat; windowEnd = targetTime + afterBeats. Positions: on-screen spread within ±35° bearing and −10..+15° pitch at 10–18 m for most types; triangles 60–150° left or right; peekers get a Wall in chart.walls. Cap concurrent targets at maxConcurrent, and never overlap strafers or holds with each other. When analysis.confidence < 0.4 (R2), slots come from detected onset peaks instead of the beat grid. The chart ends at the song's end (D12).
doneWhen: The same inputs give a deep-equal chart; a different songId gives a different one.
Over a 200-bar synthetic song, type frequencies per section kind are within ±5% of the preset matrix.
For confident analyses every targetTime lies on a beat (an eighth for burst orbs) within 1 ms; for low-confidence analyses every targetTime lies on an onset peak.
Concurrent targets never exceed maxConcurrent, and no two strafer/hold targets overlap in time.

data.title: Judge hits, track the combo and compute the 0–100 score
data.description: src/rhythm/scoring.ts: judge(songTimeOfClick, target, level) → perfect | early | late | miss, plus a signed offset in ms (D4 consequences). Combo and multiplier ×1→×4, stepping up every 8 combo points; Perfect adds 2, Early or Late adds 1, Miss resets. Decoys: a hit resets the combo and costs points; leaving one alone is neutral; decoys are left out of hit rate and vanish with no Miss. Burst hit rate counts each orb. Strafers and holds score the fraction of their life spent on target while firing; under 30% counts as a miss for the combo. Final 0–100 score plus stats: mean signed offset, hit rate per target type and max combo.
doneWhen: Unit tests cover perfect, early, late and miss at the window and Perfect boundaries.
Perfect hits raise the multiplier faster than early or late hits (test).

data.title: Define Overdrive's song, analysis and chart types
data.description: src/rhythm/types.ts holds types only, plus `as const` lists DIFFICULTIES, SECTION_KINDS, TARGET_KINDS and FLICK_SHAPES. SongMeta {id: SHA-256 hex of the file bytes, name: file name without extension, mime, duration: seconds, addedAt: ISO string, preset: PresetId, difficulty}. Analysis (T3) {version, sampleRate, duration, bpm, beats: number[] seconds, beatEnergy: number[], onsetEnv: Float32Array, onsetHop: seconds per envelope frame, confidence: 0..1}. It has no downbeats. For figures (strafer, peeker, decoy), position is the ground point and pitch is ignored. FlickTarget adds shape; BurstTarget adds orbs: {time, position}[] and counts as one target in density; Strafer, Hold and Peeker add their params. Wall {bearing, distance, width, height}. Chart {songId, preset, difficulty, level, duration, targets, walls}.

terms.meaning: The drill this plan builds (drill id 'overdrive').
An audio file the player added to their library. There is no built-in song (D11).
One pulse of the song's tempo (a quarter note in 4/4). Targets spawn and must be hit relative to beats.
A group of beats, normally four. The generator works bar by bar.
A stretch of the song (at least 4 bars, endBar exclusive). Intro and outro are positional (the first and last sections only); middle sections are classified by energy as calm, build or peak.
The timed list of targets (and walls) for one song at one preset and level. `Chart` in code.
Data that shapes a chart: target-type weights and targets per bar for each section kind, flick shape split, and optional multipliers on target parameters. `Preset` in code. MVP: Mixed only.
Easy, Normal, Hard or Expert, chosen per song. Maps to a band of drill levels (1–3, 4–6, 7–8, 9–10) that unlocks on its own (D17).
The drill's 1–10 step, as in every Azimuth drill. The chart is built at one level inside the chosen difficulty's band.
One thing to shoot that the chart spawns: a flick shape, strafer, hold, burst, peeker or decoy. `ChartTarget` in a chart.
A kind of target with its own look and behaviour (D2). `kind` on ChartTarget.
The beat a target should be hit on. `targetTime` in code (seconds of song time).
From landTime (the target lands) to windowEnd. Any hit inside counts; when it ends without a hit the target is missed and removed.
How a hit is graded: Perfect (within the Perfect width of the target beat), Early or Late (elsewhere in the window), or Miss.

Seconds into the song as the player hears it: AudioContext time since the music started, minus output latency (baseLatency + outputLatency), minus the audio offset. Everything in a run is timed from it.
The four ways the beat is shown (D5): fly-in, closing ring, pulse and the beat strip.
The Guitar Hero-style HUD strip at the bottom of the screen where icons of upcoming targets scroll to a hit line.
How late the player hears the audio, in ms. It is subtracted in song time, so a positive offset makes targets arrive later. Set by the tap-along calibration or by hand.
